rv.q: You're left with a feeling of the performer's immense set of future possibilities and that's always a good feeling to have when you walk out of the theater.
This is a charming and compelling offering at one of Chicago's most unusual small theatre spaces...
Upbeat, fast-paced and heartfelt, “Dummy in Diaspora” is both a delightful play and a capable debut work of a talented writer and performer.
What Rasho has to tell us, often with unabashed openness and wit, opens another lens on the complicated stories of SWANA American lives and families.
Still, Rasho is a true charismatic showman! He is a pure delight!!
Dummy in Diaspora will resonate with those who came from a similar background.
Rasho delivers each little anecdote as either himself, his father, his mother or others and his delivery is both “honest” and “chilling.”

cn.t: Critics praise this authentic one-man show about a gay son of Middle Eastern refugees navigating identity in America. Rasho's vulnerable, charming performance resonates across its brisk 70 minutes, though vaping onstage may distract some viewers.
